title: Affine source comparison before postcomposition with a target morphism
statement: Let R,A,R',A' and their four maps form a cartesian square of spectra [def-pc-base-change]. Let K have quasi-coherent cohomology on Spec A and L=Lg'^*K have quasi-coherent cohomology on Spec A' [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Supply a K-flat representative P with e:QP≅K and invertible pullback counit [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. For i, T is the actual global-section cohomology functor on D_QCoh(Spec A') [lem-pc-affine-derived-cohomology-presentation], F is restriction to R' followed by tilde, and H is degree-i cohomology on Spec R'. There exist a natural isomorphism d:T⋙F≅inclusion⋙Rf'_*⋙H, an A'-module U, a map a:U→T(L), and eU:F(U)≅H(Lg^*Rf_*K) such that eU.hom≫H.map(baseChange K)=F.map a≫d.hom.app L [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. At each prime p there is an additive equivalence lU:U_p≃source(r), where r is the canonical localized tensor comparison followed by tensorStalkIso, the inverse exact representative/stalk comparison and the stalk of H^i(counit inverse followed by Lg'^*e). The canonical target localization satisfies targetStalkIso(a_p(x))=r(lU(x)). There is no K', phi or target chain map, and no invertibility of r is asserted.

proof.text: Use the affine derived equivalence to represent K by a module-derived object, choose its complex preimage N, and resolve N by the actual functorial module K-flat resolution M. Map the augmentation isomorphism through the module-derived equivalence and compose its counit with the termwise tilde comparison to give e0:Q(tilde M)≅K. The module K-flat criterion implies tilde M is K-flat and its canonical pullback counit is invertible.
Apply the affine module computation to M and e0 to obtain d,U,a,eU, the global equation and local source identifications l0.

Apply source-only representative independence to the supplied P,e and tilde M,e0 at each p. Compose l0 with the resulting additive equivalence t; transitivity of the local equation gives the required square.
